question: If we start using a new outside company to power our AI features, how far ahead do customers get told?

sources.quote: The GitLab Subprocessor distribution list is leveraged to provide 30-day notice of new AI vendors.

note: The continuity plan says customers get 30-day notice of new AI vendors via the subprocessor list.

question: What uptime do we promise for our hosted SaaS site?

sources.quote: consistently maintaining our [99.95% SLA on GitLab.com]

note: Product processes cite a 99.95% SLA on GitLab.com.

question: Is it ever OK to take something that's in the free version and start charging for it?

sources.quote: we can never remove features from Core into paid tiers

note: Product principles say features can never be removed from Core into paid tiers.

question: What day of the week is the weekly growth team meeting?

sources.quote: The meeting should take place on Tuesdays for 50 min

note: The Growth page says the meeting takes place on Tuesdays for 50 minutes.

question: Which month do the big new version numbers usually come out in?

sources.quote: Our standard practice is to have the Major [release](https://about.gitlab.com/releases/) every May

note: Milestones page says the major release happens every May.

question: What app do we recommend for recording short animated screen clips on a Mac?

sources.quote: [Gifox](https://gifox.app/) is the absolute best option here, although a paid app, its reasonably priced ($14.99).

note: The GIF-making page calls Gifox the best macOS option.

question: When we plan headcount, how many product managers should one user researcher cover?

sources.quote: 1:5 ratio of UX Researchers to Product Managers

note: UX operations uses a 1:5 ratio of UX Researchers to Product Managers.

question: As a PM, roughly what share of my effort should go into really getting to know the problem before I write anything down?

sources.quote: Invest the majority of your time (say 70%) in deeply understanding the problem.

note: Product processes say to invest the majority of time, about 70%, in understanding the problem.

question: When a big customer sits down with us for their yearly exec review, how much of that meeting is the product part?

sources.quote: EBRs are usually quite long (60-90 minutes) and the product presentation is only a small portion (15-20 minutes) of the overall EBR

note: EBRs run 60-90 minutes but the product presentation is only 15-20 minutes.

question: If my team lends engineers to another team for a while, how many can we hand over and how many have to stay behind?

sources.quote: the teams who are giving shall have at least 3 engineers remaining and a maximum of 1 engineer can be given

note: PM procedures: the giving team keeps at least 3 engineers and gives at most 1.

question: What does someone have to have done in the product lately to get invited to our ease-of-use survey?

sources.quote: We use a minimum threshold of 10 product events across at least 2 stages in the previous 30 days.

note: SUS invite threshold is 10 product events across at least 2 stages in the previous 30 days.

question: When we review screens in the night-time color scheme, how weak does text legibility have to be before it gets flagged?

sources.quote: Color contrast issues where the contrast is lower than 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for graphic elements.

note: The dark mode playbook flags contrast below 4.5:1 for text (3:1 for graphics).

question: How many days in a row can I take off for a holiday?

sources.quote: Flexible time off designed to support your overall well-being, with the option to take up to 25 consecutive calendar days for vacation.

note: Flexible time off allows up to 25 consecutive calendar days of vacation.

question: When I have a baby, do I have to take my paid leave all in one go?

sources.quote: Flexible scheduling - take all at once or split into up to three segments

note: The Parental Leave Key Details list says it can be taken at once or split into up to three segments.

question: How much money a year can I get toward courses and other career learning?

sources.quote: That's why we provide up to $10,000 each year specifically for your career development.

note: General benefits provide up to $10,000 a year for career development.

question: When does my yearly allowance of coaching and therapy sessions start over?

sources.quote: Benefits reset annually on March 20

note: The Modern Health page says benefits reset annually on March 20.

question: In the US, what's the most the company will add to my retirement savings in a year?

sources.quote: **Company Match:** 50% of contributions on the first 6% of earnings (up to $1,500 annually).

note: The US 401(k) match is 50% of the first 6% of earnings, up to $1,500 a year.

question: If I quit, how long do I have to buy the company shares I've already earned the right to?

sources.quote: If a team member leaves GitLab, they have 90 days post termination to exercise their vested options. Unvested RSUs and options are forfeited upon the date of the team member's exit from the company.

note: Departing team members have 90 days after termination to exercise vested options.

question: How far above or below the middle of my pay band can salaries usually go?

sources.quote: GitLab's compensation ranges typically span from -20% to +20% of the midpoint (0.80 to 1.20 compa-ratio).

note: Ranges typically span -20% to +20% of the midpoint (0.80-1.20 compa-ratio).

question: How much can I claim for food per day while I'm away on a work trip?

sources.quote: Meals while traveling on Company business  are reimbursable, up to $120 USD (or local equivalent currency) per day.

note: Expenses policy reimburses travel meals up to $120 USD per day.

question: I'm based in the US. Do I need to keep the slip for every small thing I put on expenses?

sources.quote: US Team Members are required to only submit receipts for any expenses over $50 USD.

note: US team members only need receipts for expenses over $50 USD.

question: How much can a manager spend on flowers or a present when someone on the team has a big life event?

sources.quote: The allowable cost for gifts is up to $125 USD (including shipping) per gift.

note: Gifts are allowed up to $125 USD including shipping.

question: I work for us as a contractor outside the US. What day of the month does my money arrive?

sources.quote: the scheduled payment date is the 22nd of each month

note: Non-US contractors paid through iiPay have a scheduled payment date of the 22nd (some countries are excluded).

question: How pricey does something have to be before accounting books it as an asset instead of a regular cost?

sources.quote: GitLab establishes [$5,000 (USD)](/handbook/total-rewards/compensation/#exchange-rates) as the minimum amount required for capitalization.

note: Accounting sets $5,000 USD as the minimum for capitalization.

question: If a supplier bills us a bit more than the purchase order said, how much over is still fine?

sources.quote: All invoices are subject to a 10% PO tolerance.

note: All invoices are subject to a 10% PO tolerance.

question: After how many rounds of replying to each other in writing should we switch to talking on video?

sources.quote: Guideline: if you have gone **back and forth 3 times**, it's time

note: The guideline is that after going back and forth 3 times it's time for a video call.

question: Is it fine to join a meeting a few minutes after it's supposed to start?

sources.quote: People are expected to join no later than the scheduled minute of the meeting (before :01 if it is scheduled for :00).

note: People must join no later than the scheduled minute (before :01 for a :00 meeting).

question: How long do the messages people type into the side chat during a video call stick around?

sources.quote: Zoom Chat has been configured for a 30 day retention.

note: Zoom Chat is configured for 30-day retention.

question: My news only matters to part of the company. What share of people does it need to affect before it belongs in the main company-wide announcements channel?

sources.quote: Announcement that directly impacts less than 75% of team members

note: Announcements directly impacting less than 75% of team members should not go in #company-fyi.

question: On what date each month do we hold the meeting that starts work on the next monthly version?

sources.quote: On the 8th of each month (or the next business day), we have a kickoff meeting

note: The kickoff meeting is on the 8th of each month or the next business day.

question: How soon after talking to a candidate do I need to send in my written feedback on them?

sources.quote: It is important that scorecards are completed within 24 hours

note: Scorecards must be completed within 24 hours.

question: If I got turned down for not having enough experience, when can I apply for the same job again?

sources.quote: you are welcome to reapply to the same position once 6 months have passed.

note: Candidates rejected as insufficiently qualified may reapply to the same position after 6 months.

question: How many people should I name who can vouch for me, and does one have to be a former boss?

sources.quote: Three references will be requested and at least one needs to be a past manager.

note: Three references are requested and at least one must be a past manager.

question: If I put a friend forward for a job and they end up hired into a similar role later on, how long do I keep the credit?

sources.quote: Your referral is classified as your referral for 6 months (from the date TA receives the referral) for jobs within the same job family.

note: A referral stays yours for 6 months for jobs in the same job family.

question: How much notice does the people team need to get a new hire set up before their first day?

sources.quote: People Connect requires at least 5 days to process a new hire, but requests 10 days when possible.

note: People Connect needs at least 5 days and asks for 10 when possible.

question: At a minimum, how often should I have a one-on-one with my manager?

sources.quote: it is preferable for the manager and their direct report to have a minimum of two regularly scheduled synchronous 1-1s every month

note: The 1-1 page prefers at least two scheduled synchronous 1-1s every month.

question: In my one-on-one, how much of the talking should my manager be doing?

sources.quote: The manager should strive to do 20% of the talking while the direct report does 80%.

note: The manager should do about 20% of the talking, the report 80%.

question: Do we record the meetings where my manager's manager sits down with our team?

sources.quote: The skip level meeting is never recorded as it is a way to build trust with the team members.

note: Skip level meetings are never recorded, to build trust.

question: How far down their part of the org chart are leaders expected to know the details?

sources.quote: Leaders should know the details of their organization three levels down for efficient and effective cross-functional decision-making.

note: Leaders should know their organization three levels down.

question: How often should a manager check in with each report about whether they're happy to stay?

sources.quote: **Cadence**: Schedule your Engagement Check-In at least every 6 months with each of you direct reports.

note: Engagement Check-Ins (stay interviews) should happen at least every 6 months.

question: Which of our values comes out on top when it clashes with the others?

sources.quote: Results for Customers is at the top of our values hierarchy, as our customers achieving results drives overall business performance that enables everything else.

note: Results for Customers is at the top of the values hierarchy.

question: When we hire, are we looking for people who fit in with our culture?

sources.quote: We want a **values fit**, not a culture fit.

note: The values page says GitLab wants a values fit, not a culture fit.

question: If a change makes us more open with information but slows us down by about the same amount, do we go ahead with it?

sources.quote: If a change impacts Transparency positively but impacts Efficiency negatively in roughly the same amount, we would move ahead since Transparency is higher in the hierarchy than Efficiency.

note: Transparency ranks above Efficiency, so an equal trade-off goes ahead.

question: What's the best way to reach our chief exec if I want a quick reply?

sources.quote: I prefer Slack to email. I try to respond to every Slack message I get every day. Keep them concise.

note: The CEO prefers Slack and tries to respond to every Slack message each day.

question: If I send the head of the company an email, how long might I wait for an answer?

sources.quote: Use email when it is an external-facing communication, but don’t expect me to respond in < 1 week unless you ask me to look at it sooner over Slack

note: The CEO says not to expect an email reply in under 1 week unless asked on Slack to look sooner.

question: If I want to suggest a change to our company values, who should I send the change to for review?

sources.quote: Please assign MRs to update these values to our [Chief People Officer](https://about.gitlab.com/company/team/?department=people-group)
To update: make a merge request and assign it to the CEO.

note: The top of the values page says assign value-change MRs to the Chief People Officer, while a later section says assign them to the CEO; the page contradicts itself.

question: How much can I spend on my desk, chair and other work-from-home gear?

sources.quote: new hires will receive a 1,500 USD (or equivalent local currency) stipend to help you towards setting up your home office in your first year
Existing Team Members will get a yearly refresh of 500 USD (or equivalent local currency) to purchase upgrades, replacements, or enhancements to your home office setup.

note: New hires get 1,500 USD in their first year and existing team members get a 500 USD yearly refresh; which applies depends on tenure.

question: How long do I need to have been here to be considered for extra stock in the yearly pay review?

sources.quote: Team members may be eligible to participate in the annual refresh grant cycle review if they have completed six months of service with the company.
October 5th to be eligible to participate in the equity refresh program

note: The stock options page states a six-month service rule, while the review-cycle page gives a hire-by date of October 5; both are stated eligibility rules.

question: When I take my team out to eat, what's the spending cap per head?

sources.quote: $80 limit per person per meal.
Team meals of up to 20 people which should not exceed $100 per person

note: The expenses policy (Traveling: Team Events and Meals) caps meals at $80 per person, while the purchasing card page allows team meals up to $100 per person.

question: How much does the company put toward my pension or retirement savings?

sources.quote: **Company Match:** 50% of contributions on the first 6% of earnings (up to $1,500 annually).
GitLab contributes 4% of your basic salary
Employer matching up to 3% of base salary (maximum $2,500 CAD annually).
Team members can increase their contribution and GitLab matches up to 5% of annual base salary

note: The employer contribution depends on country: US 50% of first 6% up to $1,500, UK 4%, Canada up to 3%, Ireland up to 5%.

question: How long is the first call with a recruiter after I apply?

sources.quote: Calls can last anywhere between 30 and 40 minutes (some specialist roles require more time), depending on the conversation.
### 3. 40-Minute Screening call with a Recruiter
### **2. 30-Minute Screening call with a Recruiter**

note: The candidate FAQ says 30-40 minutes, the Support hiring page says 40 minutes and the Infrastructure page says 30 minutes.

question: On a work trip, how long do I have to be away before I can claim for getting my clothes cleaned?

sources.quote: Dry cleaning is allowable if the stay is over 5 days.
Travelers may request reimbursement for laundry for domestic travel lasting seven (7) or more consecutive days.

note: The general expenses page allows dry cleaning for stays over 5 days, while the sponsored (customer-billed) travel page allows laundry only for domestic trips of 7 or more days.

question: If I die, how much will my family get from the life cover the company provides?

sources.quote: Where local life insurance benefits aren't available, GitLab provides $20,000 in life insurance coverage that you can direct to any beneficiary you choose.
All full-time team members automatically receive life insurance coverage at 4x annual base salary through Aviva.
The automatic cover threshold for the Group Life Insurance policy is 4x base salary.

note: The default where no local plan exists is $20,000, while Ireland and the UK give 4x base salary; the answer depends on location.

question: Who has to sign off if I want to move a feature from the cheaper plan up to the pricier one?

sources.quote: The CEO is the DRI for pricing and tiers.
Requires **PLT + Required Approver approval**, mention PMM for awareness.
1. Tier-up (move from lower to higher tier)

note: The tiering guidance names the CEO as DRI for pricing and tiers, while the categories page lists tier-up changes as needing PLT plus Required Approver approval.

question: I'm launching something new and still don't know what to charge for it. Who should I talk to?

sources.quote: Contact Justin Farris's [EBA](/handbook/eba/#executive-business-administrator-team) to schedule time with the Pricing Committee (currently Sean Hall and Justin Farris)
The CEO is the DRI for pricing and tiers.

note: The launch page sends pricing questions to the Pricing Committee (Sean Hall and Justin Farris), while the tiering page says the CEO is DRI for pricing.
